references.text: Parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened." Luke 11:10 is a direct repetition of this promise.
Jesus promises that whatever you ask for in faith, you will receive – this underscores the same principle that whoever asks receives.

God promises through Jeremiah: "When you call on me and come to me in prayer, I will listen to you. You will seek me and find me." This is an Old Testament parallel to the promise that whoever seeks finds.
Wisdom says: "I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me." This is an OT promise confirming the principle that whoever seeks finds.
Moses says that if Israel seeks the Lord with all their heart and all their soul, they will find him. This confirms the promise that whoever seeks God will find him.
Jesus says: "Whatever you ask for and desire, believe that you have received it, and you will receive it." The same principle of answered prayer as in Luke 11:10.
Jesus encourages the disciples to pray in his name and promises they will receive, "so that your joy may be complete." The promise that whoever asks receives is further explained here.
John writes that "whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commands and do what pleases him." This expands on the promise of answered prayer.
James encourages asking for wisdom in faith and promises that God gives generously to all without rebuke – a confirmation that whoever asks receives.
"Seek the Lord while he may be found; call on him while he is near." An OT parallel confirming that whoever seeks God will find him.

Jesus knocks at the door and says that if anyone hears his voice and opens, he will come in. The image of knocking and having the door opened has a reversed parallel here – Jesus himself knocks and promises fellowship.
